name: North Loop
description: A former warehouse district on the Mississippi, now brick loft conversions, independent boutiques, coffee roasters and some of the city's best restaurants along Washington Avenue. It is flat, compact and walkable, with the Stone Arch Bridge and Target Field at either end. The default choice for people who want city life without a car.
bestFor: Nomads who want to walk to coffee, gyms and dinner and skip owning a car.
pros: Densest cafe and restaurant cluster in the city
Walk or bike to the riverfront and downtown
Light rail and Target Field on the edge
cons: Loud on game and concert nights
Loft conversions can mean thin walls and odd layouts

name: Northeast Minneapolis
tagline: Arts district in old industrial buildings
description: Across the river from downtown, Northeast pairs old Polish and Italian corner bars with artist studios in the Northrup King Building and a dense run of breweries along Central and University. Streets are low-rise houses and duplexes with big trees. Rents run below the North Loop for a comparable walk score.
bestFor: Nomads who want studios, breweries and character over polished new-build finishes.
pros: Best brewery and studio scene in the city
Cheaper rent than downtown or Uptown
Quick bike ride over the river to downtown
cons: Bus service is patchier than the light rail corridors
Some blocks are still industrial and bleak
Older housing stock with weak insulation

name: Uptown
tagline: Lakes, bike trails and apartment blocks
description: The area around Hennepin and Lake Street, sitting between Bde Maka Ska and Lake of the Isles. Chain of Lakes trails run right through it, so summer means swimming, running and cycling from the front door. A mix of 1920s walk-ups and newer apartment blocks, with bars, gyms and coffee on Hennepin.
bestFor: Nomads who want to swim, run or bike the lakes between calls.
pros: Chain of Lakes trails within a few blocks
Frequent buses down Hennepin into downtown
Wide mix of studios and shared houses
cons: Retail on Hennepin has thinned out with vacancies
Street parking is tight and permit-heavy
Bar noise on the Hennepin and Lake corner

name: Whittier
tagline: Eat Street and the art museum
description: A dense, diverse neighbourhood just south of downtown built around Nicollet Avenue, known as Eat Street for its run of Vietnamese, Somali, Mexican and Ethiopian restaurants. The Minneapolis Institute of Art anchors one edge. Housing is mostly older apartment buildings and subdivided houses, and it is among the cheapest central options.
bestFor: Budget nomads who want cheap food and a central address on a modest rent.
pros: Cheapest rents this close to downtown
Free art museum and good bus lines
cons: Higher property crime than the lakes districts
Some blocks feel rough after dark

name: Seward
tagline: Quiet co-op streets by the river
description: A small residential neighbourhood between the Mississippi and Hiawatha, built on Victorian houses, a long-running food co-op and the Birchwood Cafe. It is calm, tree-heavy and full of cyclists, with the Blue Line light rail and the West River Parkway trails a short ride away. Very little through traffic.
bestFor: Nomads who want a peaceful home base with river trails and easy transit.
pros: Light rail plus riverside bike trails
Good co-op groceries and neighbourhood cafes
cons: Limited nightlife, you leave for that
Housing is mostly whole houses, few studios
Freeway noise on the Hiawatha edge
